questions.question: What is considered the Root Suite in Robot Framework?

options.text: The path given to Robot Framework where it starts parsing
The first .robot file found in the directory tree
options.explanation: The Root Suite is determined by the path given to RF, not by discovery order

options.text: The directory containing the most test cases
options.explanation: The Root Suite is the starting path specified, regardless of test case count

options.text: Always the top-level directory of the project
options.explanation: The Root Suite is whatever path is given to RF, which can be any level

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Suite Files are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A Suite File must have the .robot extension
A Suite File must contain at least one test case or task
A Suite File can contain both *** Test Cases *** and *** Tasks *** sections simultaneously
options.explanation: A Suite File CANNOT contain both types simultaneously - it's either test cases OR tasks

options.text: A .robot file without test cases or tasks is still considered a Suite File
options.explanation: A file without test cases or tasks is NOT a Suite File, even with .robot extension

options.text: Suite Files are also called Low-Level Suites

questions.question: What happens when a directory path is given to Robot Framework as the Root Suite?

options.text: Only the .robot files in that specific directory are parsed, subdirectories are ignored
options.explanation: Robot Framework parses all *.robot files and directories within the path recursively

options.text: Robot Framework parses all *.robot files and directories within this path
Robot Framework only parses files named test_*.robot
options.explanation: All .robot files are parsed, not just those with specific naming patterns

options.text: Robot Framework requires an __init__.robot file to start parsing
options.explanation: No special initialization file is required to parse a directory

questions.question: What is the difference between Suite Files (Low-Level Suites) and Suite Directories (Higher-Level Suites)?

options.text: Suite Files contain test cases or tasks; Suite Directories either directly or indirectly contain Suite Files
Suite Files are always executed first, then Suite Directories
options.explanation: Execution order is determined alphabetically, not by suite type

options.text: Suite Directories cannot contain other directories
options.explanation: Suite Directories can contain other directories (nested suites)

options.text: Suite Files are written in Python; Suite Directories contain Robot Framework files
options.explanation: Suite Files are .robot files with test cases/tasks, not Python files

questions.question: How are suites ordered during execution by default in Robot Framework?

options.text: By creation date of the files
options.explanation: Execution order is not based on file creation date

options.text: By case-insensitive alphabetical order based on name and hierarchy
By file size, smallest to largest
options.explanation: File size does not affect execution order

options.text: Randomly on each execution
options.explanation: Execution order is deterministic, based on alphabetical sorting

questions.question:
Consider these file names in the same directory:

```
01__First_Suite.robot
2_Second_Suite.robot
03__Third_Suite.robot
```

What will be the suite names and execution order?

options.text: First Suite → 2 Second Suite → Third Suite
01 First Suite → 2 Second Suite → 03 Third Suite
options.explanation: Prefixes with double underscore __ are NOT part of the suite name

options.text: 2 Second Suite → First Suite → Third Suite
options.explanation: The 01__ prefix controls order but is not part of the name

options.text: All three would have identical names 'Suite'
options.explanation: Each has a different name after processing underscores

questions.question: What is the rule for using prefixes to control suite execution order without affecting the suite name?

options.text: Use a single underscore _ after the prefix
options.explanation: A single underscore is replaced by a space; use double underscore __

options.text: Add a prefix followed by two underscores __ to the file or directory name
Add a prefix in square brackets like [01]Suite.robot
options.explanation: Robot Framework uses double underscore __, not square brackets for ordering

options.text: Use a hash symbol # followed by a number
options.explanation: The hash symbol is not used for suite ordering in Robot Framework

questions.question: How are underscores in file or directory names treated when determining suite names?

options.text: All underscores are kept as-is in the suite name
options.explanation: Underscores are replaced by spaces in suite names

options.text: One or more underscores are replaced by space characters
Underscores are removed completely from suite names
options.explanation: Underscores are replaced by spaces, not removed

options.text: Only single underscores are replaced; double underscores remain
options.explanation: Double underscores after a prefix are removed; other underscores become spaces

questions.question:
Examine this directory structure:

```
Root_Suite/
├── A_Suite.robot
├── Earlier_Suite_Directory/
│   ├── B_Suite.robot
│   └── C_Suite.robot
├── Keywords/
│   └── technical_keywords.resource
└── Later_Suite_Directory/
    ├── 01__FirstSuite.robot
    └── 02__SecondSuite.robot
```

Which files/directories are considered suites? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Root_Suite directory
A_Suite.robot file
Keywords directory
options.explanation: Keywords directory contains only .resource files, no test cases/tasks, so it's not a suite

options.text: Earlier_Suite_Directory
technical_keywords.resource file
options.explanation: Resource files are not suites; they don't contain test cases or tasks

options.text: Later_Suite_Directory

questions.question: What sections are recognized by Robot Framework in suite files? (Select all that apply)

options.text: *** Settings ***
*** Variables ***
*** Test Cases ***
*** Tasks ***
*** Keywords ***
*** Comments ***
*** Imports ***
options.explanation: There is no *** Imports *** section; imports are done in *** Settings ***

questions.question: What is the correct format for section headers in Robot Framework?

options.text: Three asterisks before and after section name with Title Case separated by spaces: *** Section Name ***
Two asterisks before and after section name: ** Section Name **
options.explanation: Section headers require exactly three asterisks, not two

options.text: Square brackets with section name: [Section Name]
options.explanation: Square brackets are for test/keyword settings, not section headers

options.text: Hash symbol followed by section name: # Section Name
options.explanation: Hash symbols are for comments, not section headers

questions.question: Which sections are mandatory in a Robot Framework Suite File?

options.text: *** Settings *** and *** Test Cases ***
options.explanation: Only *** Test Cases *** or *** Tasks *** is mandatory, not *** Settings ***

options.text: *** Test Cases *** OR *** Tasks *** (one of them)
*** Settings ***, *** Variables ***, and *** Test Cases ***
options.explanation: Only *** Test Cases *** or *** Tasks *** is mandatory in suite files

options.text: All sections are optional
options.explanation: Suite Files must have *** Test Cases *** or *** Tasks ***

questions.question: What is the recommended order of sections in a Robot Framework suite file?

options.text: *** Test Cases *** → *** Settings *** → *** Variables *** → *** Keywords ***
options.explanation: *** Settings *** should come first, followed by *** Variables ***

options.text: *** Settings *** → *** Variables *** → *** Test Cases *** or *** Tasks *** → *** Keywords *** → *** Comments ***
*** Keywords *** → *** Variables *** → *** Settings *** → *** Test Cases ***
options.explanation: This order is backwards; *** Settings *** should be first

options.text: The order of sections doesn't matter in Robot Framework
options.explanation: While RF may parse any order, there is a recommended order for consistency

questions.question: In the *** Settings *** section, which of the following can be imported? (Select all that apply)

options.text: External libraries using the Library setting
Resource files using the Resource setting
Variable files using the Variables setting
Test data files using the Import setting
options.explanation: There is no Import setting; use Library, Resource, or Variables

options.text: Python modules using the Module setting
options.explanation: Python libraries are imported using Library, not Module

questions.question: Which *** Settings *** can be used to define keywords for execution flow control at the suite level? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Suite Setup
Suite Teardown
Test Setup / Task Setup
Test Teardown / Task Teardown
Suite Initialize
options.explanation: There is no Suite Initialize setting; use Suite Setup

questions.question: How can the suite name be customized in Robot Framework?

options.text: By renaming the file or directory
options.explanation: While this works, the question asks about customization beyond file names

options.text: Using the Name setting in the *** Settings *** section
Using the [Name] setting in *** Test Cases ***
options.explanation: [Name] is not a valid setting; use Name in *** Settings ***

options.text: Suite names cannot be customized; they are always derived from file names
options.explanation: Suite names can be redefined using the Name setting

questions.question:
Consider this *** Settings *** section:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Documentation    User authentication test suite
Metadata         Author    John Doe
Metadata         Version    1.2.0
Metadata         Requirement    REQ-AUTH-001
Library          SeleniumLibrary
Resource         ../resources/login_keywords.resource
Test Setup       Open Browser To Login Page
Test Teardown    Close Browser
Test Timeout     2 minutes
```

What is the purpose of the Metadata entries?

options.text: To configure test execution parameters
options.explanation: Metadata stores information but doesn't configure execution

options.text: To store additional information about the suite like author, version, or requirements
To import external data files
options.explanation: Metadata doesn't import files; it stores key-value information

options.text: To define test-level variables
options.explanation: Metadata is for information storage, not variable definition

questions.question: What is the difference between Test Setup defined in *** Settings *** and [Setup] defined in a test case?

options.text: There is no difference; they are identical
options.explanation: Test Setup applies to all tests; [Setup] applies to individual test

options.text: Test Setup in *** Settings *** defines default for all tests; [Setup] in test case overrides this default
Test Setup runs before the suite; [Setup] runs before each test
options.explanation: Test Setup runs before each test by default; Suite Setup runs before the suite

options.text: [Setup] is only for tasks, not test cases
options.explanation: [Setup] can be used in both test cases and tasks

questions.question: Which of the following settings have both a suite-level setting (in *** Settings ***) and a local setting (in individual test cases)? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Setup: Test Setup vs [Setup]
Teardown: Test Teardown vs [Teardown]
Timeout: Test Timeout vs [Timeout]
Tags: Test Tags vs [Tags]
Template: Test Template vs [Template]
Documentation: Suite Documentation vs [Documentation]
options.explanation: Documentation uses the same setting name at both levels, not prefixed with 'Test'

questions.question:
Analyze this suite file structure:

```robot
*** Variables ***
${URL}    https://example.com
${BROWSER}    chrome

*** Settings ***
Library    SeleniumLibrary
Test Setup    Open Browser    ${URL}    ${BROWSER}

*** Test Cases ***
Login Test
    Input Text    id=username    admin
    Click Button    id=login
```

What is wrong with this file?

options.text: Variables cannot be used in Test Setup
options.explanation: Variables can be used in Test Setup; this is valid

options.text: *** Settings *** section should come before *** Variables *** section
Test cases must have [Setup] defined locally
options.explanation: Test Setup in *** Settings *** applies to all tests by default

options.text: There is nothing wrong with this file structure
options.explanation: The recommended order is *** Settings *** before *** Variables ***

questions.question: What is the purpose of the *** Variables *** section?

options.text: To import variable files from external sources
options.explanation: Importing variable files is done in *** Settings ***; *** Variables *** defines variables

options.text: To define suite variables that are used in the suite, its tests/tasks, or inside keywords
To declare which variables can be modified during execution
options.explanation: *** Variables *** defines variables; it doesn't control modification permissions

options.text: To configure variable scoping rules
options.explanation: *** Variables *** defines variables; scoping is built into RF

questions.question: According to best practices, what is the most common use case for variables defined in the *** Variables *** section?

options.text: To store test results during execution
options.explanation: Variables in this section are typically for constants, not runtime results

options.text: To define constants with static values that remain unchanged during execution
To create counters that increment during test execution
options.explanation: While possible, this is not the most common or recommended use case

options.text: To define temporary variables for a single test case
options.explanation: *** Variables *** is suite-level; temporary variables are typically defined in keywords

questions.question: Why is dynamically reassigning variables defined in *** Variables *** section during execution NOT recommended?

options.text: Robot Framework doesn't allow variable reassignment
options.explanation: RF allows reassignment; it's just not recommended in this context

options.text: It may lead to test/task runtime dependencies and hard-to-debug side-effects
Reassigned variables lose their original type
options.explanation: Type handling is not the main concern with reassignment

options.text: It significantly decreases test execution performance
options.explanation: Performance is not the primary concern; maintainability and debugging are

questions.question: What is the primary difference between the *** Test Cases *** and *** Tasks *** sections?

options.text: *** Test Cases *** is for testing; *** Tasks *** is for RPA; but they are technically synonyms
*** Tasks *** can only run sequentially; *** Test Cases *** can run in parallel
options.explanation: Both execute similarly; the difference is semantic purpose, not execution

options.text: *** Test Cases *** can have assertions; *** Tasks *** cannot
options.explanation: Both can use the same keywords including assertions

options.text: *** Tasks *** requires additional installation; *** Test Cases *** is built-in
options.explanation: Both are built into Robot Framework core

questions.question: How are test cases and tasks structured in Robot Framework?

options.text: Using JSON-like key-value pairs
options.explanation: RF uses indentation-based format, not JSON

options.text: Using an indentation-based format with the name un-indented and body indented
Using curly braces to define test/task boundaries
options.explanation: RF doesn't use curly braces for structure; it uses indentation

options.text: Using XML-style tags
options.explanation: RF doesn't use XML tags; it uses space/tab-separated format with indentation

questions.question:
Consider this test case structure:

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
User Registration
    [Documentation]    Verify new user can register
    [Tags]    smoke    registration
    [Setup]    Navigate To Registration Page
    [Timeout]    1 minute
    Fill Registration Form    john@example.com    SecurePass123
    Submit Form
    Verify Success Message
    [Teardown]    Clear Test Data
```

Which elements are test-specific settings? (Select all that apply)

options.text: [Documentation]
[Tags]
[Setup]
[Timeout]
[Teardown]
Fill Registration Form
options.explanation: This is a keyword call, not a setting

questions.question: What is the difference between keywords defined in the *** Keywords *** section of a suite file versus keywords in resource files?

options.text: Keywords in suite files can only be used within that suite; keywords in resource files can be used in any suite that imports them
Keywords in suite files are faster to execute
options.explanation: Performance is the same; the difference is scope/reusability

options.text: Keywords in resource files cannot have arguments
options.explanation: Keywords in resource files can have arguments just like suite keywords

options.text: There is no difference; they function identically
options.explanation: The key difference is scope - suite keywords are local, resource keywords are reusable

questions.question: What is a common use case for defining keywords locally in a suite's *** Keywords *** section?

options.text: To share keywords across multiple projects
options.explanation: For sharing across projects, use resource files or libraries

options.text: To define suite-specific actions like Suite Setup keywords that are only relevant to that suite
To override keywords from imported libraries
options.explanation: While possible, this is not the primary use case for suite keywords

options.text: To create keywords that execute faster
options.explanation: Location doesn't affect execution speed

questions.question:
Examine this file structure:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    DatabaseLibrary
Resource    common_keywords.resource

*** Keywords ***
Setup Test Database
    Connect To Database    testdb    admin    password
    Execute SQL    DELETE FROM test_users
    
Cleanup Test Database
    Execute SQL    TRUNCATE TABLE test_logs
    Disconnect From Database
```

Is this a Suite File or a Resource File?

options.text: This is a Suite File because it has *** Settings *** and *** Keywords *** sections
options.explanation: Without *** Test Cases *** or *** Tasks ***, this is a Resource File, not a Suite File

options.text: This is a Resource File because it lacks *** Test Cases *** or *** Tasks *** section
This is invalid because it's missing required sections
options.explanation: This is valid as a Resource File; only Suite Files require *** Test Cases *** or *** Tasks ***

options.text: This is a Library File written in Robot Framework syntax
options.explanation: Library files are Python/Java code; this is a Resource File in RF syntax

questions.question: What is the purpose of the *** Comments *** section?

options.text: To define metadata about the suite
options.explanation: Metadata is defined in *** Settings ***, not *** Comments ***

options.text: To add comments that are ignored by Robot Framework and not executed or parsed
To document keywords for auto-generated documentation
options.explanation: Keyword documentation uses [Documentation] setting, not *** Comments ***

options.text: To temporarily disable test cases
options.explanation: While it could be used this way, its purpose is general comments, not test disabling
